title: Land Rover LR4 / Discovery 4
verdict: The last Discovery with a ladder frame under it, air springs that cross-link like beam axles, and low range at the twist of a dial. It's a brilliant expedition wagon wrapped round a cooling system made of plastic that's slowly giving up, so budget for that before you budget for the roof tent.

paragraphs: The Discovery 4, sold as the LR4 in North America and the Middle East, is a thorough rework of the Discovery 3 rather than a new truck. It keeps the stepped roof, the 113.6-inch wheelbase and the Integrated Body Frame, a monocoque body bolted to a ladder chassis, and adds a new face, a nicer cabin and much better engines. It is the last Discovery built that way. That makes it a seven-seat expedition truck with independent air suspension, a two-speed transfer box and Terrain Response, all for less than a used Land Cruiser. The catch is that it is still a Land Rover, and the bills arrive in plastic.

story.heading: A FACELIFT THAT WENT DEEP
paragraphs: Land Rover unveiled the Discovery 4 in the summer of 2009 and put it on sale in Britain on 1 September that year; in the US it arrived as the 2010 LR4. The nose, lamps and grille were smoothed to match the 2010 Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, and the dash was redone with a TFT driver's display and simpler switchgear. Most of the money went underneath, though: Range Rover Sport brakes, thicker anti-roll bars, a better ZF six-speed automatic, and Terrain Response retuned with a Sand launch mode and a Rock Crawl mode that brakes gently at walking pace.

The cross-linked air suspension and the electronically locking centre differential carried over from the LR3 (Discovery 3), and a locking rear differential stayed on the options list. Under the body is the same 'Integrated Body Frame' Land Rover introduced in 2004: build the passenger cell and engine bay as a monocoque, then mate it to a ladder frame that carries the gearbox and suspension. It's heavy, at about 5,600 lb for a US V8, but it's strong.

story.heading: V8, THEN A SUPERCHARGED SIX
paragraphs: In America the LR4 launched with Jaguar Land Rover's new direct-injection 5.0-litre V8, rated at 375 hp and 375 lb-ft, from the same AJ133 family that went into the 2010 [[range-rover/l322|Range Rover]]. Europe mostly got diesels: a 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6 with 600 Nm, sold from the 2011 model year as the SDV6 alongside a single-turbo TDV6, plus a basic 2.7 TDV6 that was dropped for 2011. Diesel Discoveries in Europe also got the ZF eight-speed automatic for 2012, two years before America did.

The 2014 model year changed the US truck more than any facelift did. The V8 gave way to a supercharged 3.0-litre V6 with 340 hp and 332 lb-ft, the six-speed became a ZF eight-speed with stop-start, and a lighter single-speed transfer case became standard. If you wanted low range and the active locking rear differential, you now had to tick the $1,350 Heavy Duty package, which also added a full-size spare. EPA combined economy went from 14 mpg for the V8 to 16 mpg for the V6.

story.heading: WHAT IT'S LIKE TO OWN ONE
paragraphs: Owners on LandRoverWorld and Expedition Portal tend to tell the same story. The truck is superb off-road and on a long drive, and it will tow 7,716 lb. It also eats brakes, and its cooling system is full of plastic crossover pipes and coolant manifolds that crack between roughly 50,000 and 100,000 miles. Early 5.0 V8s added a timing-chain tensioner problem, covered by Land Rover bulletin LTB00474 for 2010–2012 trucks in a published VIN range. The air suspension, meanwhile, will eventually want a compressor, a strut or a valve block.

None of that makes it a bad buy. It makes it a truck to buy with records, a scan tool and a plan. An Expedition Portal owner put it bluntly: a $14,000 LR4 can need $5,000–8,000 of deferred maintenance in the first year, and the purchase price is only the price of admission. Sort the cooling system and the chains, though, and the LR4 is far more capable on a trail than most luxury SUVs. When Car and Driver lined it up against the [[lexus/gx460|Lexus GX 460]] and three road-biased rivals in 2011, it finished fourth of five, which says more about the test than the truck.

story.heading: THE END OF THE LADDER
paragraphs: In March 2012 the one millionth Discovery came off the Solihull line, a Discovery 4, and Land Rover drove it and two sister trucks from Solihull to the Beijing Motor Show, recreating a 1950s overland expedition. That car is now on permanent display at the British Motor Museum in Gaydon. Discovery 4 production ran until 2016; owners report that the US line-up ended with Landmark and HSE Silver trims in the 2016.5 model year. Its successor, the 2017 Discovery, switched to a lighter unitary body and dropped the numeric suffix. That leaves the LR4 as the last Discovery with a separate frame under it, closing a line that began with the [[land-rover/discovery-1|1989 original]].

callout.label: SIDEBAR · JOURNEY OF DISCOVERY
callout.title: The millionth Discovery takes the long way to Beijing
paragraphs: To mark the millionth Discovery in 2012, Land Rover recreated a 1950s Solihull-to-the-Far-East expedition with Discovery 4s. The convoy crossed Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan into western China, running the desert roads from Kashgar to Korla, the stretch shown at the top of this page. The trip was raising money towards a £1 million target for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

Along the way G459 WAC, one of the pre-production Discovery 1s later converted into an amphibious vehicle, joined the celebrations at Lake Geneva. The millionth car ended the trip at the Beijing Motor Show and then went on permanent display at the British Motor Museum in Gaydon.

engineering_intro: Underneath the LR4 is the Discovery 3's Integrated Body Frame: a monocoque passenger cell and engine bay mounted to a separate ladder frame that carries the drivetrain and suspension. All four wheels are independently sprung on air struts that the computer can cross-link, so when one wheel drops, its partner on the same axle rises, as on a beam axle. Ride height runs from access height to an off-road setting with 9.4 in (240 mm) of ground clearance. Terrain Response sets throttle, gearbox, differentials, traction control and ride height for the selected surface.

engineering.note: Monocoque body bolted to a ladder chassis.
Off-road height gives 9.4 in of clearance; the Euro handbook also lists a coil-sprung 2.7 diesel.

buying_checks.head: Coolant smell, coolant top-ups, crossover history
buying_checks.body: The plastic coolant crossover pipes and manifolds are the LR4's best-known weak point on both the 5.0 V8 and the 3.0 SC V6. Owners report failures from about 50,000 miles and treat 60,000–90,000 miles as replacement time. A sweet coolant smell after a drive, a falling expansion tank or a 'low coolant' message means it's already started. Ask for invoices showing genuine crossover pipes, the water pump and the thermostat.

buying_checks.head: 5.0 V8: cold-start rattle
buying_checks.body: Land Rover bulletin LTB00474 covers a rattle or click from the front of the engine on 2010–2012 MY LR4s in VIN range AA513326–CA652214, caused by worn timing-chain tensioner levers. The fix is two tensioners (LR051008) and two levers (LR051013); the revised levers have a steel insert, and old and new parts must not be mixed. Listen to a stone-cold start, and get proof of the work if the VIN is in range. A ticking roughly once a second is more likely the fan clutch.

buying_checks.head: Air suspension: the overnight test
buying_checks.body: Raise the truck to off-road height, then check that it stays level overnight and that the compressor doesn't run constantly. A truck that sags after a few days has a leak at a strut, valve block or Voss fitting. Owners trace leaks with soapy water. If the compressor has been replaced, Arnott notes that the LR3/LR4 unit needs a software update and a new relay.

buying_checks.head: Which drivetrain do you have?
buying_checks.body: Every 2010–2013 US LR4 has a two-speed transfer box. From 2014 the base truck is single-speed with a Torsen centre differential, and low range plus the active rear locker came only with the $1,350 Heavy Duty package, which also brought a full-size spare. Owners check the 4x4 information screen (a single centre-lock icon means no HD package) and the spare, and look under the rear axle for the locker's actuator motor.

buying_checks.head: 3.0 SC V6: supercharger rattle
buying_checks.body: A rattle like gravel in a can from the top of the engine at idle is usually the supercharger's spring-type coupler isolator wearing out. A supercharger rebuilder quoted on LandRoverWorld says it starts going at around 50,000 miles. It isn't urgent, but the supercharger has to be partly dismantled or removed, so it pairs naturally with the rear coolant manifold job.

buying_checks.head: Front lower control arms and brakes
buying_checks.body: At 5,600-plus lb, the LR4 is hard on lower control-arm bushings, ball joints and brakes. Clunks over bumps, steering wander and uneven tyre wear point at the arms. Owners say brakes wear quickly and cost a lot to replace, and early trucks had a TSB for rear brake squeal when reversing.

buying_checks.head: Recalls
buying_checks.body: Run the VIN through NHTSA. Every 2010–2016 LR4 is in campaign 21V635000 for a fuel-pump flange that can crack and leak. Some 2012–2013 trucks built in August–September 2012 are in 15V386000 for panoramic-roof adhesive, and some 2015s are in 15V214000 for ABS software that can disable stability control and Hill Descent Control.

buying_checks.head: Oil changes and records
buying_checks.body: The factory oil interval was 15,000 miles. Owners on LandRoverWorld and Expedition Portal recommend 5,000–7,500 miles, and some link the 5.0 chain-guide wear to long intervals. A truck with dealer stamps at 15,000 miles and no chain or cooling work is a project priced as a driver.

repairs.title: Coolant crossover pipe, water pump & thermostat (5.0 V8)
repairs.cost: One owner's dealer bill for pump, front and rear manifolds, hoses and belts on a 2015: $5,500
repairs.symptoms: Coolant smell after driving, slowly falling coolant level or 'low coolant' warning, crusty coolant around the front of the engine or the back of the block, rising temperature under load.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant. Remove the engine covers and air intake to reach the front crossover (water pump outlet to block, LR018275) and the rear heater manifold. Pull the pipes and make sure no broken pipe ends or O-rings stay behind in the block. Clean the ports, fit new O-rings lubricated with coolant (not grease), and seat the new pipes squarely. Owners warn against cheap copies and fit genuine or aluminium parts. Replace the water pump and thermostat while you're in there, then refill with the correct 50/50 coolant and bleed the system.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets, hose-clamp pliers, pick for old O-rings, drain pan · genuine LR018275 crossover, rear heater manifold LR122709, water pump LR097165 (per Lucky8 listings), O-rings LR010800

repairs.title: Supercharger-off cooling refresh & isolator (3.0 SC V6, 2014–16)
repairs.cost: Parts plus several hours' labour; the supercharger must come off
repairs.symptoms: Coolant odour with no visible leak, slow coolant loss, a gravelly rattle from the supercharger at idle.
repairs.fix: On the SC V6 the front 'Y' crossover sits under the supercharger. Drain the coolant, remove the charge-air cooler and supercharger (it sits on two dowel pins; rock it from the snout and pry gently, minding the knock sensors underneath), then replace the front crossover (redesigned LR090630 and LR092992), the rear heater manifold, the water pump and the thermostat. One owner found his front pipe eaten away above the O-rings at 50,100 miles. Replace the supercharger coupler isolator while the blower is off. Refill and bleed the system.
repairs.tools: Metric sockets and Torx, pry bar, new gaskets and O-rings · LR090630, LR092992 front crossover, LR109401 rear manifold, LR097165 pump, LR095895 thermostat kit (one owner's DIY list)

repairs.title: Timing chain tensioners & guides (5.0 V8)
repairs.time: Land Rover allows 8.1 h for tensioners and levers; one shop quoted 18.75 h for a full chain kit
repairs.cost: Dealer quotes around $4,500 on LandRoverWorld; one full kit job was $2,346 in parts plus about $2,500 labour
repairs.symptoms: Rattle or click from the front of the engine, more pronounced at idle and most obvious on a cold start.
repairs.fix: LTB00474 calls for two new tensioners (LR051008) and two tensioner levers (LR051013). The revised levers have a steel insert, and Land Rover's follow-up note SSM71893 warns that old and new parts must never be mixed. Many independents fit the full chain kit with guides while the engine is open. The engine must be locked at the correct position with the 5.0 V8 timing tools, and the tensioners reset on reassembly. Do the water pump and crossover pipes at the same time.
repairs.tools: 5.0 V8 timing tool set, crank pulley remover/installer, torque wrench · tensioners LR051008 ×2, levers LR051013 ×2 (per LTB00474), cam cover gaskets

repairs.title: Air suspension compressor
repairs.cost: About C$1,000 quoted on LandRoverWorld; compressors run $559–889 at Lucky8
repairs.symptoms: Slow to rise, 'suspension fault' message, compressor running constantly or overheating, truck stuck at a low height.
repairs.fix: Find the leak first, or a new compressor will burn out too: raise the truck, pull the EAS fuse overnight and measure each corner, and soap-test struts, valve blocks and Voss fittings. Fit the new compressor with a new relay, and don't overtighten the Voss fittings. LR4s left the factory with Hitachi or, later, AMK units, and the EAS software must match the pump fitted, so recalibrate with a dealer tool or a GAP IIDTool. The compressor sits low beside the sill, which is why some rock sliders are designed to shield it.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands, sockets, soapy water, GAP IIDTool or dealer diagnostics · compressor (Hitachi LR023964 or AMK LR072537), relay

parts.name: LR023964H OEM Hitachi EAS compressor (LR3/LR4/RRS)
LR072537 AMK-style compressor kit (software update required)
LR4 air suspension compressor search

repairs.title: Air strut / air spring replacement
repairs.cost: Parts from about $258 for a front air spring to $509 for a complete rear strut
repairs.symptoms: One corner sags overnight, the truck leans when parked, hissing from a wheel well, bouncy ride from a leaking damper.
repairs.fix: Confirm the corner with an overnight drop test and soapy water. Support the truck on stands at the chassis, deflate the system with a diagnostic tool, disconnect the air line and height-sensor link, and unbolt the strut. Arnott advises supporting the vehicle while a new spring first inflates so the bag can't fold under, replacing springs in pairs, and checking the damper, since oil from a leaking shock can ruin a new air spring.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands, sockets, spring tools for the front strut, diagnostic tool to deflate and recalibrate · air spring or complete strut

repairs.title: Front lower control arms (bushings & ball joints)
repairs.cost: Kits $329–739 at Lucky8; one owner was quoted about C$1,200 for rear arms
repairs.symptoms: Clunk over bumps, wandering on the highway, uneven front tyre wear, torn ball-joint boots.
repairs.fix: Most owners replace the whole arm, with its bushings and ball joint, rather than pressing in new bushings. Support the truck, separate the ball joint, remove the inner mounting bolts and swap the arm. Lucky8 warns that the original bolts often rust into the arm and frame and have to be cut out, so buy the hardware kit. Finish with an alignment.
repairs.tools: Sockets, breaker bar, ball-joint separator, reciprocating saw for seized bolts · arm kit with hardware

repairs.title: Automatic transmission fluid & pan/filter service
repairs.cost: About C$1,000 at a shop per LandRoverWorld; kits $279 (six-speed) and $578 (eight-speed) at Lucky8
repairs.symptoms: Harsh or flared shifts, judder, a weeping pan or valve-body sleeve. The handbook calls the fluid 'filled for life', but owners and specialists change it.
repairs.fix: 2010–2013 trucks use a ZF six-speed with a plastic pan and integral filter; 2014–2016 trucks use the ZF 8HP70, whose LR065238 pan also carries the filter. Drain, drop the pan, replace the valve-body sleeve on six-speeds, fit the new pan, then follow the factory fill-and-level procedure, which is done at a specified fluid temperature. Several six-speed owners have switched to a steel pan with a separate filter to make future services easier.
repairs.tools: Torx and sockets, fluid pump, scan tool to read fluid temperature · pan with filter, sleeve, ZF-spec fluid

repairs.title: Brake pads, discs & parking-brake shoes
repairs.cost: Pads from about $55 (rear) and $72 (front, 2010–13); full Terrafirma kits from $328
repairs.symptoms: Wear warnings, vibration under braking, squeal when reversing (early trucks had a TSB for rear squeal), a weak electronic parking brake.
repairs.fix: Pads and discs are conventional: retract the piston, swap pads with new wear sensors, and replace discs if they're under minimum thickness or lipped. Owners note the rear-squeal fix works best with new rotors as well as pads. The parking brake uses shoes inside the rear disc. Inspect them whenever the discs are off, and follow the workshop-manual procedure for the electronic parking brake before you work on them.
repairs.tools: Sockets, caliper piston tool, torque wrench, diagnostic tool for EPB service mode · pads, discs, sensors, EPB shoes

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: US trucks came on 255/50R19 or 255/50R20. On the 20s, LandRoverWorld owners say 265/50R20 fits at standard height without rubbing and is the largest size that still fits the spare well when fully inflated. A 285/50R20 rubs slightly at full lock and needs the spare deflated to fit underneath. Owners who switch to aftermarket 18-inch wheels run 265/65R18 with no rubbing at standard height; 285/60R18 brings only mild liner rub at full compression or lock.

The 2010–2013 V8 makes 375 hp and 375 lb-ft and has a two-speed transfer box as standard, but 2010–2012 engines in the bulletin's VIN range can need timing-chain tensioners. The 2014–2016 V6 makes 340 hp and 332 lb-ft, gets the eight-speed and a better EPA rating (16 vs 14 mpg combined), but has its own supercharger-isolator and cooling-pipe issues, and needs the HD package for low range.

faq.q: Does my LR4 have low range and a rear locker?
faq.a: All 2010–2013 US LR4s have the two-speed transfer box. Owners disagree on whether every 2010–2013 truck also got the rear locker, so check physically or with a VIN decode. For 2014–2016, low range and the active rear locker came only with the Heavy Duty package ($1,350), which also included a full-size spare.

faq.q: Is the 5.0 timing-chain problem a deal-breaker?
faq.a: No, if it's been done or priced in. Bulletin LTB00474 covers 2010–2012 LR4s in VIN range AA513326–CA652214, and the fix is new tensioners and steel-insert levers (8.1 hours of labour by Land Rover's own timing). Owners believe later 2012 and 2013 engines got the updated parts from the factory, and many stress shorter oil-change intervals.

faq.q: How often should I replace the coolant crossover pipes?
faq.a: There's no factory interval, but owners treat them as a maintenance item: failures are reported from about 50,000 miles, replacement every 60,000 is considered cautious, and past 100,000 miles original pipes are 'borrowed time'. The SC V6 can overheat quickly once coolant is lost, so don't ignore a coolant smell.

faq.q: What oil does it take, and how much?
faq.a: The 5.0 V8 takes SAE 5W-20 meeting WSS-M2C925-A, about 8.0 litres (17 US pints) with the filter. Land Rover's 2014 service bulletin also specifies 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A for the SC V6, and owners say 2015–16 handbooks call for 0W-20 to STJLR.51.5122. The oil level is shown electronically rather than on a conventional dipstick, and most owners extract the old oil from the top and change the cartridge filter on top of the engine.

The advertised maximum is 7,716 lb (3,500 kg) braked, and the gross train weight is 14,859 lb. One LandRoverWorld owner tows a 6,600-lb boat and trailer and came away impressed. The Discovery 4 also added Trailer Stability Assist.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: EPA ratings: 12/17 mpg city/highway (14 combined) for the 2010 V8, 13/17 for 2013, and 15/19 (16 combined) for the 2014–2016 SC V6, all on premium. An Expedition Portal V8 owner averages about 14 mpg. The petrol tank holds 86 litres (23 US gal).

faq.q: Can I lift it and keep the air suspension?
faq.a: Yes. Lift rods that replace the height-sensor links, such as Proud Rhino's PR25, raise it about 2.5 in with no reprogramming. One LandRoverWorld owner found that strut spacers with 18-inch wheels drove far better than lift rods with wheel spacers. If you're done with air altogether, Terrafirma sells a +2 in air-to-coil conversion.

faq.q: Which scan tool do owners use?
faq.a: The GAP IIDTool is the common choice. Owners use it to reset ride height and to match the EAS software to a replacement Hitachi or AMK compressor. A generic OBD-II reader can't do those jobs.
Land Rover quotes 700 mm (28 in) at off-road height and 600 mm (24 in) at standard height.

faq.q: Was the diesel sold in the US?
faq.a: No. US LR4s were petrol-only: the 5.0 V8 for 2010–2013 and the 3.0 SC V6 for 2014–2016. The TDV6 and SDV6 diesels were sold elsewhere.

mods.why: Longer height-sensor links trick the air suspension into riding about 2.5 in higher with no programming. Coil conversions trade air's adjustability for simplicity.

baseline_service.intro: Most LR4s are now past 100,000 miles on a 15,000-mile factory oil interval, and the handbook calls the gearbox 'filled for life'. Baseline everything, and treat the cooling-system plastics and the air suspension as part of the service, not as optional extras. Fluid specs below are from Land Rover's Discovery 4 owner guides; check your own handbook for 2014–16 SC V6 figures.

items.spec: 5.0 V8: SAE 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A, 8.0 L (17 US pt) with filter · 3.0 SC V6: 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A (2014 TSB); owners report 0W-20 to STJLR.51.5122 for 2015–16, ≈8 L [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.interval: Then every 5,000–7,500 mi (owner practice; factory interval was 15,000 mi)
items.note: Cartridge filter (LR011279) sits on top of the engine; the housing is marked with its torque (25 N·m). Most owners extract the oil from the top.

items.interval: Pressure-test now; crossover pipes, manifolds, pump and thermostat at 60,000–90,000 mi if undocumented (owner practice)
items.note: This is the LR4's weakest system. Replace the expansion-tank cap too, and use genuine or aluminium pipes rather than cheap copies.
